verdict.note: Development transfer evidence. Silence from a failure is not a pass; an unanalyzed fixed twin fails.

what_failed: All three comparisons exhausted a 3000-second deadline and produced no artifact, so there is no target evidence at all. The engine reports `cpg batch taint failed` twice per case on the 1,274-file PMPro tree: first with an exception whose trace runs through ujson array transformation, then by timeout on the retry.
harness_defects_found: The first run selected one case of three: the manifest labels a case by what it is (vulnerable, fixed, benign) while the id says what the comparison does (introduce, repair, benign), and the harness filtered on one while keying expectations by the other. Its all-false verdict was a harness defect, not a transfer result.

The second run's timeout was a per-query ceiling of 300 seconds, which the runner takes as the minimum with the remaining transaction time. Raising only the deadline could never have helped, and did not.
reading: This is a runtime blocker on a large repository, not evidence about whether the design transfers to PHP. The pins, source receipts and declared target are all correct, so the question was asked properly and the engine could not answer it within any budget tried. PHP transfer stays unestablished and M3 stays unmet.
limits: No detection, precision or admission claim for PHP: nothing completed to claim anything about.
